Collection Description
# 👋 Welcome - start here Thanks for taking a look. This collection tests the e-commerce API end to end, and it is written so you can understand it by reading it, without opening a single script. Everything below takes about two minutes. --- ## Step 1 - make sure you imported both files There are two, and you need both: | File | What it is | |---|---| | `ecommerce-api-tests.postman_collection.json` | the tests (this file) | | `ecommerce-api-environment.postman_environment.json` | the settings they use | ## Step 2 - select the environment Top right of the Postman window there is a dropdown that says **No Environment**. Change it to **"E-Commerce API - Test Environment"**. > This is the only setup step, and it is the one people forget. If you see every > request failing with a strange address error, this dropdown is why. ## Step 3 - press Run Click the collection name in the sidebar → **Run** → **Run E-Commerce API - QA Test Suite**. The suite is 42 requests and 187 checks. The whole thing takes about 20 seconds. **There is nothing to fill in first.** No tokens to paste, no product ids to look up, no users to create by hand. The first folder registers its own accounts, logs them in, and stores the tokens automatically. Everything after that helps itself. --- ## 🟥 Please read this before you judge the results **Exactly 20 checks fail on purpose.** The suite is not broken - those failures are the whole point. The tests check what the API is *supposed* to do, not what it currently does. So each real problem shows up as a **failing test**, instead of being quietly recorded as if it were correct behaviour. Every request that is meant to fail is named `[BUG-1]`, `[BUG-2]` and so on, and the number points at the write-up in **BUGS.md**. > **The rule that matters: anything that fails WITHOUT a `[BUG-n]` tag is a genuine > new problem.** As of the last run there were none. --- ## 📖 How to read the request names | If the name starts with | It means | |---|---| | nothing special | A normal test. It should pass, and it does. | | `[BUG-n]` | ❌ **Fails on purpose.** It proves problem number `n` is real. | | `[QUESTION-n]` | ⚠️ Passes. Something I want a decision on, not a bug I am certain of. | | `[BY DESIGN]` | ✅ Passes. Looks like a bug, is not one. Explanation on the request. | ## 📂 What the folders do | Folder | What it covers | |---|---| | **01 - Setup** | Registers the users and saves their tokens. **Run this first.** | | **02 - Register** | The email rule, both sides of the password rule, duplicate sign-ups | | **03 - Log in** | Whether a password is really checked. The worst problem lives here | | **04 - Products** | The list, one product, and the description rule | | **05 - Orders: permissions** | Tokens, and whether an order is actually yours | | **06 - Orders: bad data** | Bad baskets, bad quantities, unknown products, broken JSON | | **07 - Orders: totals & stock** | Totals, stock levels, and ownership | Every folder and every request has its own **description tab** - like this one - explaining what it checks and why that is worth checking. Start there. --- ## ⚙️ The settings, if you want to change anything All of these live in the environment file. You will not normally need to touch them. | Setting | What it is for | |---|---| | `baseUrl` | The address of the API. **Change this one value to point the whole suite at a different environment.** | | `seededUserEmail` / `seededUserPassword` | The login for `alice@qa.com`, who the API already has | | `aliceOrderId` | An order that belongs to alice (`o-1001`) | | `bobOrderId` / `bobUserEmail` | An order belonging to somebody else (`o-1002`), for the ownership tests | Everything else - the test accounts, their tokens, product ids, prices, stock levels - is worked out while the suite runs and cleaned up after itself. Nothing is typed in by hand, which is deliberate: this data is held in memory and resets from time to time, and a suite full of hard-coded ids would stop working the first time that happened. --- ## 🐛 What it found Nine problems. Three of them are serious. | # | In one line | How serious | |---|---|---| | 1 | **You can log into anyone's account without their password.** | 🔴 Critical | | 2 | **Any customer can read any other customer's orders.** | 🔴 Critical | | 3 | **Buy 10 of something, get charged for 1.** | 🔴 Critical | | 4 | You can buy more of an item than the shop has. | 🟠 High | | 5 | Some products promise a description and do not have one. | 🟡 Medium | | 6 | A quantity typed as text is accepted and stored. | 🟡 Medium | | 7 | Stock never goes down, no matter how much is sold. | 🟡 Medium | | 8 | One error returns a web page instead of an error message. | 🟡 Medium | | 9 | `Alice@qa.com` and `alice@qa.com` are two different people. | 🟢 Low | Each one is explained in plain English in **BUGS.md**, with a single command you can paste into a terminal to see it happen yourself.
